pr.author: cjgillot

analysis.summary: DestinationPropagation's live-interval construction only marked Def/PartialWrite places live in the second half of a statement, so reads inside aggregate rvalues were treated as dead by the statement's twostep. That allowed unification of an aggregate's destination local with a local read by the aggregate, producing self-overlapping aggregate assignments (e.g. a tuple swap rewritten as `_1 = (_1.1, _1.0)`), which clobbers values needed by later fields. The fix marks Use places live through the statement by default, except for simple `_a.stuff = {copy|move} _b.stuff` assignments with identical projections, where marking the rhs local live would block intended unification.
analysis.originalLogic: In `save_as_intervals`, for each statement the pass appended a `twostep` interval and marked written-to locals live in the second half of the statement. The old statement visitor matched `DefUse::for_place` and inserted the `twostep` value only for `DefUse::Def | DefUse::PartialWrite`; `DefUse::Use` and `DefUse::NonUse` were ignored. Thus statement reads were assumed to finish before the statement's second half, and a local read by an rvalue could appear dead before the statement completed. (Terminators already treated reads as conflicting with writes by that terminator.)
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Because reads inside an aggregate statement were not kept live through the statement, DestinationPropagation could unify the aggregate destination local with a local read by that same aggregate. For a swap-like sequence `_2 = copy _1; _1 = (_2.1, _2.0)`, it could propagate so the aggregate becomes self-overlapping, e.g. `_1 = (_1.1, _1.0)` (or the equivalent on the unified destination), instead of keeping `_2` distinct. Such an overlapping assignment interleaves reads and writes of the same local: writing one field destroys a value still needed to read another field, so a swap can yield `(old_field1, old_field1)` rather than `(old_field1, old_field0)`. The historically incorrect transformation is therefore "unify a local read by an aggregate with that aggregate's destination, yielding an overlapping aggregate assignment"; the corrected pass forbids this while still permitting unrelated unifications and the simple same-projection copy/move exception.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions (post-borrowck, during DestinationPropagation) containing statements whose rvalues interleave reads and writes, especially `Rvalue::Aggregate` with multiple field operands, plus `Rvalue::CopyForDeref` / `Rvalue::Use`. The bug is reachable when an aggregate destination local is a unification candidate with a local read in the same statement, e.g. tuple-field swaps or re-wrapping a scalar into a tuple. Custom MIR (`#[custom_mir(dialect = "runtime")]`) is used upstream to construct these exact shapes.
analysis.trigger: DestinationPropagation computes a local's live interval as ending before the second half of a statement even though that local is read later within an aggregate assignment, so it unifies the aggregate destination with the read local and creates an overlapping assignment.
preconditions: DestinationPropagation is running and the destination local is otherwise eligible for unification with a local read in the same statement.
The statement's rvalue interleaves reads and writes, canonically `Rvalue::Aggregate` such as `_1 = (copy (_2.1), copy (_2.0))`; the fix says to treat statements as behaving so by default.
Under the old marking scheme, the read local's interval ends before the statement's second half because only Def/PartialWrite places were marked at `twostep`.

The fix's exception applies only to simple assignments where `lhs.projection == rhs.projection`; those must remain unifiable, so a test must not globally forbid all statement reads from being marked live.
pitfalls: Do not conflate intra-statement overlapping reads/writes (aggregate operand aliasing) with post-copy overwrites or borrowing restrictions; they are separate conditions.
Legal unification can still happen across a copy, e.g. `_1.0 = 0; _0 = copy _1` becoming `_0.0 = 0; nop`; the `nop` is expected and not evidence of the bug.
The fix deliberately exempts `_a.stuff = {copy|move} _b.stuff` with equal projections because marking `_b` live there would prevent unification; do not describe that exception as the bug.
A retained test name or old comment does not establish correctness; compare actual value assignments and which locals appear on each side of the aggregate.
Do not assume the pass should leave the program untransformed: it may still unify disjoint locals; only the overlapping unification is wrong.
The old and new outputs can differ in which local carries the initial constant (e.g. `_1` vs `_0`); focus on whether the aggregate destination aliases a local read by the aggregate.
analysis.testStrategy: Add MIR-opt tests using `//@ test-mir-pass: DestinationPropagation`, `EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`, and `// EMIT_MIR <name>.DestinationPropagation.diff` for both panic strategies. Construct custom MIR with `#[custom_mir(dialect = "runtime")]`; use CHECK lines to assert that a swap-like aggregate keeps a distinct source local, e.g. `_0 = (copy (_2.1: ...), copy (_2.0: ...))` with `_2 = copy _0`, and that the aggregate is not rewritten as `_0 = (copy (_0.1), copy (_0.0))` or `_1 = (copy (_1.1), copy (_1.0))`. Include a scalar rewrap case to confirm legal unification still occurs (`_1` unified into `_0`, followed by `nop`). Keep a separate simple same-projection copy/move case to guard the exemption from over-marking reads live.
